visualBrief: Almería’s hilltop Alcazaba, with its rounded Christian bastions, crenellated taifa garden enclosures, Muro de la Vela, and stepped Jayrán wall to Cerro de San Cristóbal.

photoFacing.frontBasis: The castle remains east–southeast of its western rounded bastion along the three mapped enclosures. The Jayrán rampart turns northeast toward Cerro de San Cristóbal. The local frame is east/south.

limitations: The Christian castle footprint, rounded towers, site paths, garden boundary, pool and Jayrán wall are available in PMTiles. Other wall thicknesses, lower terrace alignments and tower heights are interpreted from the aerial and ground photographs.
The model covers the extant exterior, including the three enclosures and the Cerro de San Cristóbal wall. Interior rooms and recent temporary restoration equipment are outside scope.
Walls and sills fit the standard Terrarium terrain samples. Precise ground contact, local grades and small archaeological remnants depend on the terrain and mapped detail available to the host.
terrain: Bilinear six-meter sampling from standard zoom-15 Terrarium tiles.
